title: App Builder Capability and Provider Registry
description: Governance record for the non-LLM execution capabilities the factory might buy rather than build, and the provider candidates that would be benchmarked against each one. Registration is not adoption and adoption is not readiness. This schema validates config/capability-providers.json; it is not a contract family, because nothing executes against it and generating types for a boundary with no second side would be a type nobody imports.

criticality.description: quality-critical: a published product's quality depends on it, so it needs more than one benchmarked provider before it reaches a launch path. quality-supporting: its absence degrades a result rather than blocking one. optional: recorded so the architecture does not exclude it, with no consumer.

ownedContract.description: The artifact App Builder keeps when the provider is replaced. Without this the capability is a purchase rather than a contract.

contractRequirements.description: Capability-specific, deliberately. A raster brief and a crawl request share governance but not shape, and one interface spanning both would describe neither.

deterministicAlternativeFirst.description: The cheaper route that must be shown insufficient first. Principle 1 in machine-readable form.

adoption.description: candidate: registered for a benchmark. conditional-candidate: enters the benchmark only if a stated speciality is first demonstrated to be needed. incumbent: the in-repository route others must beat. adopted: won a named benchmark task. rejected: considered and declined.

ready.description: Whether this route is usable today. False for every external provider by construction; true only for an in-repository incumbent that already runs.

priceBasis.description: How the provider charges, in units rather than amounts. Rates a budget must enforce belong to the budget at run time.

credentialRef.description: Where a trusted gateway would look. Never a value.

candidateFor.description: The task classes this provider is registered to compete on. Selection is per task; a provider that wins one has proved nothing about the others.
